mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% (as of t-1mo) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points (as of t-1mo) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening economic activity, triggering negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO decline in the last 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Residential fixed investment above 500,000 million dollars (as of t-2mo) indicates strong housing market demand, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns in late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS exceeds 500,000 million dollars during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 105 (as of t-2mo) indicates slowing manufacturing output, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO is below 105.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.5% (as of t-1mo) signals rising inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust labor market and consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through elevated corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST increase in the last 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising), higher discount rates reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising).
